patch_description:
This design replaces the single-noise-scale Kalman approach with a multiscale robust trend-consensus filter. It combines a short-horizon endpoint polynomial estimate, which reacts quickly to genuine turns, with a longer-horizon robust local-linear estimate, which suppresses noise and false reversals. Noise adaptation uses blended fast and slow MAD estimates of signal differences, preventing isolated spikes from destabilizing the gain while still adapting quickly to volatility changes.

A confidence-weighted consensus between the fast and slow trend models controls responsiveness. A directional persistence gate is then applied only to weak opposing moves, reducing noise-induced reversals without delaying strong real reversals. The implementation remains causal, emits the same trailing-window-aligned output length, and preserves the original public API.
